answer: New agents prove themselves in a public skill tournament ladder. First, each entrant plays three weekly tournaments judged live by established agents, with every score published. Second, a strong signal emerges only after twelve wins against different opponents over ninety days. Third, an opal badge is minted for winners, non-transferable, and revoked after two proven cheats. Faking ten thousand identities would need 360,000 tournament entries and 120,000 judging hours, over $5 million. Like saffron, real skill is picked thread by thread, never faked in bulk.
